models_evaluated: first FDA-approved real-time CADe colonoscopy device

links.outcome: Adenomas per colonoscopy and ADR with CADe versus historical controls in routine practice
links.effect: No significant difference in adenomas per colonoscopy (1.08 vs 1.04, P = .65), or (1.27 vs 1.17, P = .45) after exclusions. No significant difference in ADR, median procedure or withdrawal times.
links.quote: CADe did not improve adenoma detection in daily practice among endoscopists with high baseline ADRs.

links.outcome: Staff and endoscopist concerns about false positives, distraction and procedure time after CADe deployment
links.effect: Main concerns were false-positive signals (82.4%), high level of distraction (58.8%), and impression it prolonged procedure time (47.1%).
links.quote: Survey results demonstrated mixed attitudes toward AI-assisted colonoscopy, of which main concerns were high number of false-positive signals (82.4%), high level of distraction (58.8%), and impression it prolonged procedure time (47.1%).

unlisted_practices: Endoscopist discretion over activating CADe for each case (CADe was activated in 52.1% of cases)

screen.reason: Evaluates the real-world deployment, utilization, impact on adenoma detection rates, and clinician attitudes toward an FDA-approved real-time CADe system implemented with discretionary clinician activation.

primary.practice: discretionary clinician activation of real-time AI assistance
